info.name: Ecommerce API - Frontend Handoff
info.description:
This collection provides runnable REST requests and saved Laravel responses for frontend integration. Tokens in saved examples are placeholders.

## Getting started

1. Import the collection and set baseUrl. The default is http://localhost:8000 on the Docker host.
2. Check API health, then register a customer or sign in with a seeded account. Sign-in saves tokens by role. Test logout after finishing the other session requests.
3. Connect categories and products, then the cart, checkout, and order details. Use IDs returned by the API in Postman variables.
4. Use an admin token for admin requests. If Postman asks for an image file, select main-app/laravel/database/seeders/fixtures/phone.png from the project root.

Seeded accounts are available after running the command below from the project root with the services running and migrations applied. To give the first registered customer ID 1, register them before seeding.

~~~powershell
docker compose exec -e INVENTORY_GRPC_TIMEOUT=10000000 app php artisan db:seed
~~~

## Response contract

- Send Accept: application/json. For JSON bodies, send Content-Type: application/json. Protected endpoints use Authorization: Bearer <token>.
- Successful responses include success, message, and data. Paginated responses add links and meta. Follow links.next when present. An empty page returns an empty data array.
- Errors return success set to false, a message, and data set to null. Validation errors map each field in errors to a list of messages. Other errors can return errors set to null.
- Amounts such as price, total_amount, unit_price, and subtotal are decimal strings. Quantities and IDs are integers. created_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp.
- Catalog images are absolute URLs. Cart image paths are relative to /storage/. Set Laravel's APP_URL to a URL the browser can reach.

| HTTP | Frontend handling |
| --- | --- |
| 200 and 201 | Render data and update local state |
| 401 | Check credentials on login. Sign in again for protected requests |
| 403 | Show the required permission |
| 404 | Show that the resource is unavailable |
| 409 | Refresh stock and the cart after a checkout conflict. For product creation, check the key and request data |
| 422 | Show field errors or the general message for cases such as a rejected order transition |
| 429 | Ask the user to wait before another login attempt |
| 500 and 503 | Show a temporary error. After a checkout failure, check the order list and cart before retrying |

## Browser integration

The local Docker setup was tested with a preflight from http://localhost:5173 using Authorization, Content-Type, and Idempotency-Key. Check CORS settings when the frontend origin or deployment changes. Cross-origin JavaScript needs Retry-After exposed to read it.

The API covers authentication, the catalog, admin product management, the cart, checkout, and order management. The server manages inventory, and order details expose the current status.

Checkout creates an order and reserves stock. Payments, notifications, and admin restocking require additional endpoints.

item.name: 00 Connection
item.description: Check the Laravel URL before connecting the frontend.

request.description: Checks that Laravel responds over HTTP. data.status is ok. Read the details of a published product to check inventory connectivity.

response.name: 200 Laravel reachable

item.name: 01 Authentication
item.description:
Registration and login return a JWT in data.token and the user in data.user. Send Authorization: Bearer <token> for protected requests.
Call GET /auth/me to restore a frontend session. Use user.role to select the customer or admin views. Laravel enforces permissions.
Sign in again after a token expires or a protected request returns 401. The default JWT lifetime is 60 minutes when JWT_TTL uses its default value.
Successful requests save sessionToken for profile and logout and save customerToken or adminToken based on the user's role.

request.description:
Send name, email, password, and password_confirmation as JSON. Name and email are limited to 255 characters, and the email must be unique. The password must contain at least eight characters and match its confirmation. Public registration assigns the customer role. Omit role.
A 201 response returns the user and token. A 422 response provides field errors. Change registerEmail for a new registration.

response.name: 201 Customer registered
422 Missing required fields
422 Email already in use

request.description:
Send email and password as JSON. A 200 response returns data.user, data.token, and data.token_type set to bearer.
A 401 indicates invalid credentials. A 422 indicates invalid fields.
Login allows five attempts per minute per IP. On 429, wait and honor Retry-After when available to the browser.

response.name: 200 Customer session
401 Invalid credentials
422 Invalid input
429 Login limit reached

request.description:
Send email and password as JSON. A 200 response returns data.user, data.token, and data.token_type set to bearer.
A 401 indicates invalid credentials. A 422 indicates invalid fields.
Login allows five attempts per minute per IP. On 429, wait and honor Retry-After when available to the browser.
Admin login uses the same endpoint. The admin role comes from data.user.role. Postman saves the token in adminToken for admin requests.

response.name: 200 Administrator session
401 Invalid credentials
429 Login limit reached

request.description: Requires a Bearer JWT. data.user includes id, name, email, role, and created_at. Ask the user to sign in again on 401.

response.name: 200 Customer profile
200 Admin profile
401 Missing token
401 Logged-out token rejected

request.description: Send an empty body and a Bearer JWT. A 200 response returns data set to null and revokes the current token. Clear the local session token after logout.

response.name: 200 Session ended
401 Missing token

item.name: 02 Catalog
item.description: These endpoints are public. Use categories for filters, the catalog for product listings, and product details to check available stock.

request.description: Lists categories by name with 15 results per page. Accepts page. Each category includes id, name, and a nullable description.

response.name: 200 Category list

request.description:
Optional parameters are page, per_page, and category_id. per_page ranges from 1 to 50 and defaults to 12. category_id must reference an existing category.
The response includes a data array, links, and meta. Use meta to select a page or follow links.next. Pagination links preserve the category and page size.
Each product includes id, name, description, price as a decimal string, image as an absolute URL, a category object, and created_at. Read product details for stock. An empty page returns 200 with an empty data array.

response.name: 200 Filtered catalog page
200 Empty catalog page
422 Invalid page size

request.description:
Use a catalog ID for productId. The response adds integer available_quantity to the product fields. Zero means out of stock. Availability can change before checkout.
image is ready to use in an img element. Laravel builds the URL from APP_URL.
A 404 means the product is unavailable for display. On 503, stock could not be read and the UI can offer a retry.

response.name: 200 Product in stock
200 Product out of stock
404 Product not found
503 Inventory temporarily unavailable

item.name: 03 Cart
item.description:
The cart belongs to the authenticated user. Each cart operation returns data.id, data.items, and data.total_amount.
Each line includes its own id, product, quantity, and subtotal. Use the line id for PUT and DELETE.
Cart product.image is a relative path such as products/file.png. Prefix it with the Laravel URL and /storage/. Catalog image URLs are absolute.
Use the decimal strings in total_amount and subtotal. Checkout reserves stock.

request.description: Requires a Bearer token. Render data.items and data.total_amount. An empty cart returns 200 with an empty items array and a total of 0.00.

response.name: 200 Cart with items
200 Empty cart
401 Missing or expired JWT

request.description: Send product_id for a published product and an integer quantity from 1 to 1000. If the product is already in the cart, the quantity is added. A 201 response returns the full cart.

response.name: 201 Item added
422 Quantity validation error

request.description: Send an integer quantity from 1 to 1000 to replace the previous quantity. A 200 response returns the full cart. A 404 means the line is missing or belongs to another cart.

response.name: 200 Quantity replaced
422 Quantity validation error
404 Cart item unavailable

request.description: Send an empty body. A 200 response returns the full cart after removal. A 404 means the line does not exist in the current cart.

response.name: 200 Item removed
404 Cart item unavailable

item.name: 04 Customer Orders
item.description:
Checkout starts with the current cart. Display its API total before sending POST /orders when the customer confirms.
On success, open order details using data.id and refresh the cart. Order items include the product name and price at purchase.
Valid statuses are pending, confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, and cancelled. Admins can update the status.

request.description:
Requires a Bearer token and an empty body. Laravel calculates the total from the account's cart and reserves stock. A 201 response returns a pending order and clears the cart.
A 422 with errors.cart indicates a cart problem, such as an empty cart. A 409 means the stock reservation was rejected. A 503 means the inventory service could not complete the request.
Disable repeat submissions while the request is running. After a connection error, check the cart and order list before retrying.

response.name: 201 Order placed
422 Empty cart
409 Insufficient stock
503 Inventory temporarily unavailable

request.description:
Returns the current user's orders newest first, with 10 results per page. Accepts page and returns data, links, and meta.
Each order includes id, status, total_amount as a decimal string, items, and created_at. An empty order list returns 200.

response.name: 200 Customer order history
200 No orders yet

request.description:
Use an ID from checkout or the order history for orderId. Items include id, product_id, product_name, unit_price, quantity, and subtotal.
A 404 means the order is missing or belongs to another customer. Display the current status from data.status.

response.name: 200 Order details
404 Order unavailable to this customer

item.name: 05 Admin
item.description:
Use adminToken from admin login. A 403 means the role lacks permission. A 401 means the token is missing or invalid.
Create a disposable product with a fresh productCreationKey before trying product edits or deletion. The create request saves adminProductId for those requests.
Follow the allowed transitions in Update order status.

request.description: Use a catalog ID for productId. Admins can use the public product details endpoint to read stock in data.available_quantity. Zero means out of stock. On 503, show that stock is temporarily unavailable and retry the details request.

response.name: 200 Product in stock
200 Product out of stock
404 Product not found
503 Inventory temporarily unavailable

request.description:
Send JSON with a unique name of up to 255 characters. description is optional and can be null.
A 201 response returns data.id, data.name, and data.description. On 422, show errors.name next to the name field.

response.name: 201 Category created
422 Name already exists
403 Admin role required

formdata.value: A smartphone for everyday photography and communication.

request.description:
Send multipart/form-data with category_id for an existing category, name up to 255 characters, price from 0.01 to 99999999.99 with at most two decimal places, initial_quantity as an integer from 0 to 2147483647, and image as a file. description is optional.
Accepted images are JPG, JPEG, PNG, and WebP up to 5 MiB. In a browser, use FormData and let the browser set Content-Type and its boundary.
A 201 response returns the product and image URL. Read product details for available_quantity. A 422 response includes field errors such as errors.image.
Idempotency-Key can be up to 255 characters. Use a new key for each new product, and reuse the same key, fields, and file when retrying that creation. A change in the payload with the same key returns 409. A 503 can leave a product pending initialization. Retry with the same key to finish.
In Postman, change productCreationKey when creating a different product and select the image fixture if prompted.
The create request saves the returned ID in adminProductId for the edit and delete requests.

request.description:
Send only the fields you want to change. Use null to clear description. The category_id must exist, name accepts up to 255 characters, and price must be from 0.01 to 99999999.99 with at most two decimal places.
A 200 response contains the updated product. Stock is managed separately. A 422 response contains field validation errors. A missing, deleted, or unpublished product returns 404.

response.name: 200 Product updated
422 Invalid product fields

request.description:
Send multipart form data with _method=PATCH and the image file. Select postman/fixtures/product.png if prompted. Accepted images are JPEG, PNG, and WebP up to 5 MiB.
You can include category_id, name, description, or price in the same request. Let the client set Content-Type and the multipart boundary. Read the new image URL from data.image.

response.name: 200 Product image replaced

request.description:
Use the adminProductId from a disposable product. A 200 response returns data set to null. The product disappears from the catalog and carts while existing order history and reservations are preserved.
Refresh the catalog after success. A repeated delete, or a missing or unpublished product, returns 404.

response.name: 200 Product deleted
404 Product unavailable

request.description: Uses the order history endpoint with an admin token. Lists all orders with 15 results per page and accepts page. Each order includes id, status, total_amount, items, and created_at.

response.name: 200 Administrator order list

request.description: An admin token can read any order. Set orderId from the order list. The response has the same data fields as customer order details.

response.name: 200 Administrator order details

request.description:
Send status as JSON. Show only transitions allowed from the current status.

| Current status | Allowed transitions |
| --- | --- |
| pending | confirmed or cancelled |
| confirmed | processing or cancelled |
| processing | shipped or cancelled |
| shipped | delivered |
| delivered | Final state |
| cancelled | Final state |

A 200 response returns the updated order. Shipping commits the stock reservation and cancellation releases it. A 422 indicates an invalid value or a disallowed transition. Field errors are in errors.status, while a disallowed transition can return errors set to null. A 503 can occur during shipping or cancellation if inventory is unavailable. Read the order status again after a connection failure.

response.name: 200 Order confirmed
422 Invalid status value
422 Invalid status transition
403 Admin role required
503 Inventory temporarily unavailable
